newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - April 25.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - April 25.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - The market slowed to digest earlier purchases, leaving prices flat to lower in most species but failing to stem the advance in Southern Pine, Random Lengths said in its weekly update. Western S-P-F was hit the hardest and, while some mills resisted the pressure, a few others sold aggressively, it said.
Treaters were a major source of orders for southern mills, but some buyers who could use untreated wood turned to lower-priced western and Canadian species, Random Lengths said.

Dealers played the market cautiously, taking prompt shipments when they could find them, often at the secondary level but avoiding extended deliveries. Distributors walked a fine line, trying to keep enough wood on hand to supply their customers fill-in needs but limiting replacements at current prices. Wholesalers took a defensive posture. Those who owned wood concentrated on reducing their bought-ahead positions, often at less than replacement costs, Random Lengths said.
Other wholesalers had success filling customers' specific needs when they could connect with mills who were flexible.

Price resistance by dealers and foul weather in some markets got part of the blame for the slower pace. Transportation remained a headache for both buyers and sellers. Rail shippers in the western half of the continent complained of their inability to get empties. Meanwhile, buyers continued to trace loads hung up by weather in the middle of the continent. Rail cars and trucks were in tight supply in some areas of the south but the situation was more a nuisance than a critical problem.
Canada exports as of April 17 were at 4.5 percent of quota.
